name: nonhuman-fc1
origin: efc1 tranche (Flux ma59y73); scripts ported from test-results/experiments/efc1/scripts/{build,run,assets,analyze}.py — spec docs/research/fun-control-input-surface.md §3.2
measures: Estimator round-trip keypoint error vs each arm's control keypoints (mean/median px, % of frame diag, % of subject-bbox diag, p50/p90), detection counts, manual vision tags (quadruped rendered vs humanized vs envelope-only), wall-clock.

fixtures.scene: portrait room crossing, 39f @ 480x832, res_multistep + simple shifts 12/3, guidance 1.0 (BasicGuider), turbo OFF, caches OFF

prompts.dance: A dancer moves across the room.
prompts.dog: A dog trots across the room.
prompts.creature: A strange tall creature walks across the room.

fixtures.inputAssets: testbed input/efc1/ (source frames, control renders, authored humanoid skeleton, sprite composite — derived by assets.py)

estimatorCatalogIds.ap10kPose: AP-10K rtmpose-m torchscript (fetches on first use via pack ckpts — recorded in the fetch log)

A.label: human baseline — DWPose render of the dance clip -> Fun Control (the path that must work end-to-end)

B.label: AP-10K quadruped skeleton of the dog trot -> Fun Control (the topology question)

C.label: authored humanoid skeleton riding the dog torso trajectory (format-vs-semantics control)

D.label: sprite/region composite of the dog along the trot path (the shipped-workaround ceiling)

candidateSlot.description: A candidate CONTROL METHOD or SKELETON FORMAT: a prebuilt control-video frame folder + the estimator used to score it (dwpose body-18 or ap10k 17), or an alternative fun-control recipe (strength/endPercent/steps). Slots in against arms A (human parity) and D (workaround ceiling).

slotFields.controlDir: testbed input subdir with f%06d.png control frames (control-video)
slotFields.estimator: dwpose | animalpose — which estimator scores the round trip (control-video)

rubric.contact: Contact sheet of a room-crossing generation. Tag: (1) is a QUADRUPED rendered with proper quadruped articulation (never a bent human, never a draped spectral figure)? (2) does it follow the left-to-right crossing path? (3) pose fidelity vs the control render: stride/limb placement plausibility.

limits: Round-trip error conflates control adherence and estimator noise; the human baseline A calibrates the floor (measured: A 13.9-26.0 px).
Estimator torchscripts load to CUDA outside ComfyUI management — the estimator-restart rule applies between phases (restart or free_verified slack 900 MiB before sampling).
The resolution=480 trick (k=1 on 480x832) is what keeps AP-10K keypoint JSON in native pixel coordinates — do not change resolution without remapping.
Single subject class (dog); AP-10K covers more, untested here.
